qc.label_under_test: In code (Python, JavaScript, Java, C++ and similar), a list or array being started, typed or grown: strongest for an empty list literal or empty list constructor that is about to be filled, a List/ArrayList/vector type or type hint, or adding one item to the end of it (append, push); a list literal that already holds items fires more weakly, and so does technical prose saying something returns a list or array. Dicts, sets, tuples, plain numbers and 'list' in everyday prose stay quiet; a variable only named with 'list' can fire weakly.

neighbours.label: In code (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C++ and similar) and technical prose, a value that is a list or array, whether it is being built or only used: strongest for an empty list or array literal about to be filled and for a list/array type or type hint, but it also fires on adding an item to a list, on expressions or calls that produce a list, on reading, passing or looping over a variable that holds a list (often a plural name), and on prose saying something returns or holds a list or array. The same code with a dict, set, tuple, string or single number or object stays quiet. The word 'list' alone (in everyday prose, or in a variable name whose value is not a list) fires weakly to moderately.
